metaTitle: Draft WhatsApp Shopify Flow Workflows with Sidekick
metaDescription: Use Sidekick to draft an inactive WhatFlow workflow in Shopify Flow. Review the selected trigger, order context, branches and recipients before activation.
answer: Use Shopify Sidekick on desktop to draft an inactive Flow workflow from a precise event, condition and intended action. Then inspect the actual WhatFlow Business API tasks, recipient variables and order references in Flow. Keep the draft inactive while checking positive, nonmatching and repeated-event cases; the generated diagram and configuration screenshots do not establish message delivery.
takeaways: Describe the intended business rule and explicitly request an inactive draft.
Select a missing WhatFlow task manually rather than accepting a substitute.
Review generated fields and branches separately from any later delivery check.
practicalParagraphs: Beside the inactive draft, record three lines: requested rule, actual selected steps and remaining gaps. For the supplied DELIVERY_INFO demo, inspect the exact text condition and fromPhoneNumber recipient. Keep the separate order-tagging exercise in its own note so a colleague does not mistake the demonstrated text workflow for a completed order-confirmation process.
checklist: Keep the generated workflow inactive during review.
Confirm the installed trigger and recipient variable in the editor.
Check false, repeated-event and missing-data cases.
Record which checks inspect logic and which would require a separate controlled end-to-end exercise.

metaTitle: Connect WhatsApp and Shopify Apps with Flow Tasks
metaDescription: Compose WhatFlow WhatsApp workflows with compatible Shopify app tasks. Check connector requirements, recipient lookups and ownership before enabling a blueprint.
answer: Connect WhatFlow Business API to another Shopify app through Flow when the installed apps expose compatible triggers and actions and supply the identifiers each step needs. Verify the connector setup, any separate plan requirement and the recipient mapping. Treat the guide’s app combinations as blueprints; the inactive screenshots do not prove that every third-party route has executed.
takeaways: An app listing or integration logo does not expose every feature as a Flow task.
A customer ID needs a supported recipient lookup before a WhatsApp send.
Third-party app plans remain separate from WhatFlow’s all-feature plans.
practicalHeading: Record the missing field before extending a blueprint
practicalParagraphs: For the documented Judge.me blueprint, write down the paid-plan and Send Verified Trigger requirements beside the installed event. Then record that its inspected variables omit a buyer phone number. Leave the draft inactive until a supported lookup supplies the intended permitted recipient; the order.phone mapping in a different screenshot is not a completed solution to that gap.
checklist: Confirm the exact installed trigger and action.
Verify third-party plan and connection requirements.
Map every required identifier and recipient field.
Assign one owner to the reminder schedule and exception path.

metaTitle: Send WhatsApp Templates from Shopify Flow with WhatFlow
metaDescription: Configure WhatFlow Send WhatsApp Template in Shopify Flow. Match an approved template, recipient and variables to the event, then review missing data and duplicates.
answer: To configure a WhatsApp template in Shopify Flow, choose an event supplying the required data, add WhatFlow Business API’s Send WhatsApp Template action and map the intended recipient. Use the exact approved template name, language and matching variables. Review missing values and repeated events while inactive; an accepted Flow step is not proof of delivery or reading.
takeaways: Choose the event around what the message can truthfully establish.
Map only the variables required by the actual approved template.
Keep request acceptance, delivery and reading as separate outcomes.
practicalHeading: Compare the approved preview with each mapped input
practicalParagraphs: For the inactive six-placeholder order-confirmation demo, keep the approved preview beside the Flow editor and label each input by its meaning: name, order number, subtotal, total, address and city. Check currency formatting and missing-value handling at the same time. The sample template name belongs to the documented demo; use the approved structure from your own account.
checklist: Confirm the actual template approval, name and language.
Choose a recipient field and handle missing phone data.
Match every input to its placeholder and formatting needs.
Check duplicate notifications and split-fulfillment behavior.
Keep the sample inactive until configuration review is complete.

metaTitle: Route Incoming WhatsApp Messages in Shopify Flow
metaDescription: Build a narrow WhatsApp first-response workflow with WhatFlow and Shopify Flow. Map the sender, review keyword conditions and leave clear paths for team help.
answer: Route incoming WhatsApp messages in Shopify Flow by selecting WhatFlow Business API’s text-message trigger, checking a narrow condition and mapping the reply recipient from the incoming sender field. Keep order changes on an order-aware path. Review nonmatching text, repeated messages and human handoffs while inactive, and use free-form replies only within the applicable customer-service window.
takeaways: An incoming sender number is not a resolved Shopify order.
Start with a narrow request condition before broadening intent matching.
An invitation to reply TEAM does not itself assign a colleague.
practicalHeading: Give the sample keyword an explicit no-reply case
practicalParagraphs: Keep DELIVERY_INFO as the exact controlled condition in the inactive demonstration. Add a review note showing that an unrelated complaint should not receive the sample delivery-policy answer. Replace the sample delivery estimate with the store’s maintained policy before any later use, and name the inbox process that handles TEAM rather than implying an assignment action already exists.

metaTitle: Tag Shopify Orders from WhatsApp Confirmation Replies
metaDescription: Use WhatFlow WhatsApp Order Reply in Shopify Flow to match the configured answer and tag the correct order. Review negative replies, older messages and repeats.
answer: Use WhatFlow Business API’s WhatsApp Order Reply trigger when a customer’s response must update an identified Shopify order. Match the reply type and the configured button text or payload, then add a meaningful tag to the order supplied by that trigger. Keep nonmatching replies for review and test repeats and older messages without treating confirmation as automatic fulfillment authority.
takeaways: Use the order-specific trigger rather than a generic button event.
Match the actual configured answer before adding an order tag.
A confirmation tag does not itself authorize charging, refunding or fulfillment.
practicalHeading: Write expected results for the same buyer’s two orders
practicalParagraphs: For a hypothetical review case, give one controlled buyer two test orders and an older confirmation message. Record which order each reply is expected to reference before inspecting the inactive workflow’s mapping. Add a repeated-tap case with the expected already-handled behavior. This checks the association and business rule rather than assuming that a familiar confirmation label identifies the newest order.
checklist: Confirm WhatsApp Order Reply supplies the intended order reference.
Match the real reply type and configured button value.
Select the trigger’s order in the tagging action.
Review negative, typed, repeated and older-message replies.
Keep the demo inactive and consequential actions outside this tagging recipe.

metaTitle: WhatFlow and Shopify Flow: WhatsApp Automation Guide
metaDescription: Build WhatsApp automations visually with WhatFlow and Shopify Flow. Choose incoming triggers, message actions and clear conditions, then review an inactive workflow.
answer: Build a WhatsApp automation visually by selecting a Shopify or WhatFlow Business API trigger, adding a condition and choosing a supported action in Shopify Flow. Match the event’s data to the intended outcome and message rules. Start with an inactive, narrow workflow; inspect logic and field mapping before any separate controlled check of an actual external action.
takeaways: A trigger supplies context, a condition selects a branch and an action performs the task.
Choose order-aware events for order work and eligible formats for messages.
All WhatFlow Business API plans include features and no inbox seat fees; allowances and rates differ.
practicalHeading: Choose the next recipe by the outcome you need
practicalParagraphs: Use a short routing exercise when the aim is to recognize a question and prepare a relevant reply. Use the order-reply recipe when the aim is to record an answer against a specific order. Keep these as separate inactive drafts initially so the team can see which fields each trigger provides and avoid mistaking a sender number for an order reference.
checklist: Write one event, one rule and one intended outcome.
Inspect the selected trigger’s actual fields.
Map the recipient or target order from the proper context.
Check missing data, repeats and a human exception path.
Record that built-in test previews do not prove delivery.
